review.review: The run ended with a living, full-health hero and a stuck planner, not an observed death (decision 313, log line 970). Gas-room supplies remained unresolved, so mandatory potion discovery correctly refused to spend unknown colors as unrelated strength tests. An earlier supply opportunity was incorrectly excluded: crystal-branch valuation could not traverse ordinary closed doors, although normal navigation could. This hid already observed potion rewards behind doors 444/520 while a crystal key was held. Original-source offline bookkeeping reconstruction matched recorded actions 0–312 and reproduced the terminal blocker; this is reconstructed memory, not recorded memory. A focused correction makes branch valuation admit ordinary closed-door transit under the existing safety checks. The new regression failed on original source and passed with the correction; all 1,768 suite tests passed, with four skipped. Candidate reconstruction first changed decision 265 (log line 828), selecting an approach to the crystal branch; reconstruction stopped there. This establishes an available preparation choice, not potion acquisition, identity, gas-room success or survival.
review.learnings: Evaluate observed crystal-room rewards through ordinary closed transit doors before abandoning a held key. Keep supply conservation, fresh potion-test safety checks, actual protection verification and pickup receipts separate: choosing a supply approach is not completing the puzzle.
